1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Peñaseca for three days. In spring, Lucía Romero's older sister had left for Madrid, and since then Lucía had been running the little village apothecary on her own.
At nightfall, she closed the shutters, counted what she had earned that day, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely gone to bed when someone knocked hard at the door downstairs. A man's voice asked, "Is anyone there?"
In the doorway stood a young man soaked to the bone, his left arm wrapped in a bloodstained cloth. He said his name was Diego Lobo and that he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need to be healed," Lobo said in a low voice. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred reales be enough?"
He took a letter wrapped in waxed paper from his jacket. "This letter must reach the monastery of San Blas before the eighteenth of May."
For Lucía, healing that wound was child's play, but the letter troubled her.
Even so, she did not accept his money and only said, "Tomorrow at dawn I will take you to the mountain."
2: At daybreak they set off. Lucía carried on her back a basket with bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope they met old Tomás Gil, who was splitting firewood. He set down the axe and told them in a low voice that the previous afternoon three strangers had asked at the entrance to the village about a wounded young man.
"Go by the path, Lucía," said Tomás Gil. "The main road isn't safe." Lucía thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Lucía went ahead, planting her feet firmly with each step. Lobo followed her in silence.
At noon the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and in the distance the roof of the monastery of San Blas appeared. At the door a nun was waiting, Sister Inés, in charge of receiving visitors.
Sister Inés took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting 2 years for this letter."
Lobo said to Lucía, "I owe you my life." Lucía smiled: "Then, next time you come, fix the roof of the apothecary for me." Lobo stayed at the monastery.
At dusk, Lucía came down the mountain alone. When she got home it was already night; she lit the lamp and sat for a long time behind the counter.
